title: Autoscaler metric-noise regression — 95th-percentile latency spikes causing scale oscillation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a high-traffic period on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated autoscaler oscillations causing a temporary capacity shortage and elevated tail latency for hosted API customers. The autoscaling system aggressively scaled up and down in response to short-lived 95th-percentile latency spikes propagated by a noisy internal metric stream (ingress latency histogram). This ticket documents the investigation, root cause, immediate mitigations, and follow-up actions.
impact: For ~90 minutes multiple customer routes saw 95th-percentile request latency double and some requests hit request timeouts. A subset of small-mid customers experienced transient errors; enterprise customers with dedicated capacity were unaffected. Estimated revenue impact: low-medium but high operational load for SRE and support teams.

root_cause: A recent telemetry change (PR #4120) changed the aggregation pipeline for request latency histograms to emit a 95th-percentile estimate with lower smoothing. That change made short-lived latency spikes more visible to the scaling system. The KEDA scaler we use was configured to scale based on the 95p latency signal with a short evaluation period (30s) and no debouncing. The combination of increased signal sensitivity and short evaluation window caused the autoscaler to treat transient jitter as sustained load, leading to repeated scale-ups followed by rapid scale-downs as spikes resolved, resulting in cold-starts and elevated tail latency.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Temporarily increased KEDA scaler evaluation window to 2m and added 3m debounce on scale-down. 2) Rolled back the telemetry smoothing change on the aggregation pipeline for 95p latency to previous safe default while tests ran. 3) Enabled HPA CPU fallback for affected deployments so that a different, less noisy signal could prevent under-provisioning.
long_term_mitigation:
1) Change autoscaling signals: prefer smoothed percentiles or moving-window percentiles for KEDA triggers; use a composite signal (95p smoothed + CPU moving-average) with majority vote to decide scaling actions.
2) Implement scale-debounce and hysteresis defaults in our autoscaler config library and surface them in Console.
3) Introduce a synthetic warm-pool for cold-start sensitive routes and make warm-pool size configurable per route.
4) Add regression tests and chaos tests for metric noise and cold-start scenarios to the autoscaling test-suite.
5) Update telemetry ownership and change-review checklist to require autoscaler impact assessment for any change to latency aggregation/percentile code.
